rationale: mutation_score=0.667 is below the 0.5 threshold in spirit acceptable numerically but validation_status=fail and three requirements (FR4, SR4, SR5) are uncovered/undetected by their own mutants, despite the mutants genuinely reintroducing the corresponding defects. For SR4, the mutant submission lists only benign, unrelated decoder gates (u_minterm3, u_sel2_we) as trigger/payload and omits the true bridging instances (g_alias_tap_and, g_alias_or2) entirely -- this is exactly the kind of wrong/irrelevant suspect_nets entry SR4 is supposed to catch, yet evaluate.py's SR4 check passed it. For SR5, the mutant submission fabricates a false second anomalous address (001) with unsupported claims of bank1_we/bank3_we co-assertion, which exhaustive simulation ground truth would contradict -- yet evaluate.py's SR5 check passed it. For FR4, the mutant submission makes a blanket claim that the alias behavior potentially affects all four legal addresses (000, 001, 010, 011) by listing per-address benign select gates as payload, violating the single-address scoping FR4 mandates -- yet evaluate.py's FR4 check passed it. In all three cases the mutant content is a valid, non-defective corruption of the correct answer, so the checks themselves are too weak/permissive and must be strengthened, not the mutants.
revision_instructions: Strengthen three requirement checks in evaluate.py so they actually discriminate correct submissions from corrupted ones (all three checks currently pass corrupted answers that a correct answer would not produce): (1) SR4 check: it must verify that suspect_nets contains at least one entry whose net_name/gate_instance structurally matches the actual bridging gate(s) responsible for driving the address-011 minterm signal into the bank2_we enable tree with role 'trigger' or 'payload' -- cross-check by tracing, from the reported net/instance, through the netlist's structural connectivity to confirm it actually feeds bank2_we and is gated on the address-011 decode condition; a submission that lists only ordinary per-address decode gates unrelated to the bridging structure (e.g. the plain minterm decoder or the legitimate bank2 select gate) without naming the actual extra bridging instance(s) must FAIL. Do this via structural data-flow tracing on decoder_netlist.v, not by matching specific hardcoded names, so a differently-named-but-correct golden still passes. (2) SR5 check: it must cross-validate every claim in suspect_nets/affected_outputs/evidence against the exhaustive simulation ground truth (all 8 addresses x 2 write_en values via testbench_harness.v) and FAIL if the submission asserts anomalous multi-write-enable behavior at any address other than the one identified in trigger_condition -- a submission that adds a second fabricated anomalous address not present in the exhaustive trace must FAIL, even if the primary address/outputs are still correctly reported. (3) FR4 check: it must FAIL when suspect_nets or evidence assign trigger/payload roles to multiple distinct per-address decode gates spanning more than the single trigger address (i.e., when the submission implies the bridging behavior could manifest at more than one address), not just when trigger_condition itself lists multiple addresses. Verify against the mutant behavior: a submission naming several unrelated per-address select gates as payload while making blanket-scope statements about all addresses violates FR4 and must be rejected. Ensure the mutation_baseline_run (golden) still passes all three strengthened checks.
